atoms.text:
Undocumented migrants are people who do not have legal permission to enter a country or stay in it. This level explores several tragedies in which undocumented migrants died while trying to reach or work in Britain.

Trigger warning: the texts mention death, exploitation and human trafficking.

atoms.b: Each of the 58 migrants had paid around £20,000 to be ((smuggled)) into Britain.
The victims in the Dover lorry had ((suffocated)) after being trapped in a sealed container for more than 18 hours.
The lorry driver was sentenced to 14 years for ((manslaughter)), not murder, because the deaths were not planned.

instruction.text: Listen to the news and fill in the gaps.

atoms.a: <voice voiceLang='de' voice='custom'>instrument-tubular-6</voice> It's February 5th, 2004. Welcome to today's news. Less than four years after 58 Chinese migrants were found dead in a lorry, 23 Chinese cockle pickers have drowned in Morecambe Bay after being cut off by a rising tide. They had been trafficked into the UK by Liverpool-based gangmasters, spoke little English, and had never seen the sea before. Their gangmaster was found guilty of manslaughter and jailed for 14 years.
atoms.b: 23 Chinese workers drowned in ((Morecambe_Bay)) on the northwest coast of England.
The workers had been illegally employed as ((cockle_pickers)), gathering shellfish from the shallow waters of the bay.
The victims had been trafficked into the UK by Liverpool-based ((gangmasters)), who controlled every aspect of their lives.

instruction.text: What happened afterwards? Put the events in the right order.

atoms.text: 23 Chinese cockle pickers drown in Morecambe Bay after being cut off by the tide
Gangmasters Licensing Authority (GLA) created in 2005 to regulate labour suppliers

hint.text:
to prosecute – verfolgen
to revoke sth. – etw. widerrufen/entziehen
hint.sound: <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>to prosecute</lang> bedeutet verfolgen. <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>to revoke something</lang> bedeutet etwas widerrufen oder entziehen.
hint.label: Vocabulary

atoms.b: Any business acting as a ((gangmaster)) must apply for a licence, and the GLA has the power ((to_inspect)) workplaces, investigate complaints and prosecute unlicensed operators.
If a gangmaster is found to be underpaying workers, confiscating their passports, housing them in ((unsafe)) conditions or charging them illegal fees, the GLA can ((revoke)) their licence.

end.text:
Despite these laws, tragedies continued.
For example: In October 2019, 39 Vietnamese people were found dead in a refrigerated lorry trailer in Grays, Essex. Eleven people were later convicted in the UK and 19 in Belgium.
end.sound: Despite these laws, tragedies continued. For example: In October 2019, 39 Vietnamese people were found dead in a refrigerated lorry trailer in Grays, Essex. Eleven people were later convicted in the UK and 19 in Belgium.

atoms.b: The laws dealing with human ((trafficking)) and forced labour were spread across several different pieces of legislation, making them ((difficult)) to enforce. The Modern Slavery Act (2015) brought all of these rules together into a single stronger ((law)), which criminalises human trafficking as well as ((forced_labour)) and domestic servitude.
